advisory.finding: The `_plan_review_variant` docstring claims 'When the light read fails the fingerprint is `None` and the variant is the literal `material=None`', but `current_material_fingerprint` → `current_material_fingerprint_impl` re-raises (does not return None) on a pinned-ticket-read failure when a pinned view is active, so in that case the variant computation raises rather than degrading to `material=None`.
scenarios: A plan review start/sync issued while an immutable pinned ticket view is bound and the pinned read fails

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the plan-review dedup fingerprint and the material the review body reads the same snapshot (pass the fingerprint/material into work() instead of re-reading), so an edit cannot land between the two reads.
evidence: Shared mutable resource: the ticket's plan material/description, read as `current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:83) which fetches `current_plan_context(ticket_id)` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:484).

≥2 executors: review_plan_start offloads to a worker thread `await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(lambda: _start_gate_job(...))` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:267); sync review_plan runs in an executor thread calling `run_gate_singleflight(...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:455); the new tests additionally interleave `rebar.edit_ticket(...)` as a third mutator (tests/unit/test_mcp_llm_dedup.py after_edit coroutine).

Interleaving window — READ#1: `variant=_plan_review_variant(ticket_id, source)` -> `return f"source=...;material={current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id)}"` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:83), used to build the dedup key in `compute_key(...)` under `_lock` (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:252, 307; _attach_or_create at :167-174).

Interleaving window — READ#2: the leader runs `work()` = `_review_plan_body(...)` -> `rebar.llm.review_plan(ticket_id, ...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:96) inside `_run_leader` (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:202), entirely OUTSIDE `_lock`; the review independently re-reads the description, so the fingerprint keyed into dedup and the material actually reviewed are two non-atomic reads.

Concrete harm: a follower that read material M1 attaches (via `_attach_or_create` returning leader=False, src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:170) to a leader that reviewed M2, so the author polls/consumes a verdict for a plan version they did not request — the same stale-plan harm the commit targets, narrowed to the fingerprint-read-vs-review-read window rather than eliminated.

ABSENCE rationale: `_lock` (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:167) covers only key registration, not the fingerprint read nor the later review read, so the two reads are not serialized against an intervening edit.
advisory.finding: The plan-review dedup key reads the material fingerprint (READ#1) at a different, earlier time than the review body re-reads the plan material (READ#2), so an edit landing between the two reads lets a run keyed on the old material actually review the new material (or vice versa) — the leader can be keyed on fingerprint M1 while review_plan reviews M2, and a follower that read M1 attaches and polls findings for a plan that was not the one reviewed.
scenarios: An author edits the ticket description during an in-flight plan review; the edit lands after _plan_review_variant computed the fingerprint but before review_plan reads the description.
Two near-simultaneous starts where edit_ticket interleaves between the first start's fingerprint read and its review body's material read.
